items.stem: An agent implements a feature but the spec was ambiguous about an edge case. What is the root issue?

options.text: The specification left an ambiguity the agent could not resolve correctly on its own
options.rationale: Correct: ambiguous specs produce unreliable agent output.

options.text: The agent model was too small
options.rationale: The gap is in the spec, not model size.

options.text: Agents cannot write code at all

options.rationale: Language choice is not the cause.

items.explanation: Correct: ambiguous specs produce unreliable agent output.

items.stem: Which TWO qualities make a requirement suitable for an AI coding agent? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It is unambiguous about expected behaviour

options.rationale: Correct: testable criteria let you verify output.

options.text: It is written as a single huge task
options.rationale: Large undifferentiated tasks are hard to review.

options.text: It omits edge cases to save space
options.rationale: Omitting edge cases invites wrong behaviour.

items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Why decompose a feature into small tasks for an agent rather than one large one?

options.text: Smaller increments stay reviewable and limit the blast radius of mistakes
options.rationale: Correct: incremental, reviewable changes are safer and easier to verify.

options.text: Agents charge per task so it is cheaper
options.rationale: Cost structure is not the reason.

options.text: Large tasks are impossible for any model
options.rationale: Possible but harder to review and verify.
Decomposition does not remove the need for tests.
